content.title: About
content.content: Pumpernickel muffin is a small baked good made from whole‑grain rye flour, often sweetened with honey or sugar, and served as a snack or dessert. It has a dense, slightly moist crumb, a distinctive rye aroma, and a gentle sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpernickel is a traditional German rye bread that serves as the base for these muffins.
The dark color comes from whole rye grains and sometimes the addition of molasses.
Muffins are frequently topped with cream cheese frosting or sprinkled with pumpkin seeds.
In the United States, pumpernickel muffins are especially popular during the autumn season.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Rye flour provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Pumpernickel releases sugar more slowly, helping maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Rye supplies B1, B3, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains magnesium, iron, and zinc, supporting muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Rye muffins contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, a serving can be calorie‑rich; moderation is advised.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions may increase the risk of tooth decay if consumed frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy a pumpernickel muffin as a standalone snack, split it and spread cream cheese, crumble it into yogurt, or use it as a base for open‑face sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 3 months).
